senses.d: To help (somebody) to survive, or rescue (somebody or something) from harm.
ex: She was saved from drowning by a passer-by.

Thou hast[…]quitted all to save / A world from utter loss.

senses.d: To spare (somebody) from effort, or from something undesirable.
ex: I'll save you / That labour, sir. All's now done.

senses.d: To redeem or protect someone from eternal damnation.
ex: Jesus Christ came to save sinners.

senses.d: To catch or deflect (a shot at goal).

senses.d: To conserve or prevent the wasting of.
ex: Save electricity by turning off the lights when you leave the room.

ex: Where did I save that document? I can't find it on the desktop.

senses.d: An instance of preventing (further) harm or difficulty.
In various sports, a block that prevents an opponent from scoring.
ex: The goaltender made a great save.

senses.d: A successful attempt by a relief pitcher to preserve the win of another pitcher on one's team.
ex: Jones retired seven to earn the save.

senses.d: A point in a professional wrestling match when one or more wrestlers run to the ring to aid a fellow wrestler who is being beaten.
ex: The giant wrestler continued to beat down his smaller opponent, until several wrestlers ran in for the save.

senses.d: An action that brings one back out of an awkward situation.
ex: Nice save.

senses.d: The act, process, or result of saving data to a storage medium.
ex: If you're hit by a power cut, you'll lose all of your changes since your last save.
